messages:
Alex: CI nightly failed on the flash-attn packaging job for paged/fused kernels. Error happens during wheel build in container image.
Alex: paste of the failing snippet:
```
ERROR: nvcc fatal   : Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_86'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcuda
gcc: error: unrecognized command line option '-Wno-reserved-user-defined-literal'
```
Maria: ugh, that nvcc arch error usually means the base image's CUDA toolkit is older than what our build flags expect. Which image is CI using?
Alex: it's using rwi/toolchain:ci-ubuntu20.04-cuda11.1 (we switched it in a patch last month). The kernel build expects CUDA 12.1 in some branches (we added compute_86 and a few flags).
Sam: also seeing the `-Wno-reserved-user-defined-literal` GCC complaint — GCC 9 doesn't know that flag. That lines up with ubuntu20.04 default gcc=9.
Jin: this explains the intermittent packaging failures on the fused-attn variant matrix. When the toolchain image is ubuntu22.04 + gcc11 + cuda12 we pass, but the older image fails. CI matrix covers both and only one shard fails which makes the nightly red.
Olga: action: we should either pin compile flags to the lowest common denominator or pin the toolchain image per kernel variant. I vote for pinning images in CI and adding a fast smoke compile for all variants.
Alex: profiling context: we also saw a perf regression on production after we deployed the new kernel selector — it picked flash-attn-v2 for seq=512 small batch cases and latency increased ~9%. That selection was based on the microbench numbers which were measured on machines with gcc11/cuda12. Packaging mismatch might produce subtly different kernels and microbench numbers.
Maria: good point. Build environment differences can change fortran flags, optimization codegen and so change perf. We need reproducible compiler/toolchain for perf numbers.
Sam: concrete PRs: 1) CI: pin base images for kernel build to ubuntu22.04/cuda12 for flash-attn variants; 2) add a quick compile-and-run microbench step in CI that builds a tiny kernel and runs a fixed set of inputs (seq 64/512/2048, batch 1/8) and dumps perf numbers; 3) cache compiled artifacts between CI runs (s3 cache) to avoid long builds.
Jin: I'll open the PR to pin images + matrix update. For compatibility we should add a fallback build (force compute capabilities to a minimal set: 50,60,70) so non-CUDA12 GPUs still produce a wheel.
Olga: For packaging, add build-time detection: if nvcc version < 12 then force-remove compute_86 flag and fallback to older code path (paged attention). Keep the CI smoke test to verify both paths.
Alex: can we also make the runtime kernel selector aware of build-time metadata? e.g., include kernel build tag in the wheel (cuda/gnu versions) so the routing policy can avoid selecting a kernel variant that wasn't validated on this toolchain. That would have prevented the regression.
Maria: yes, add a ``build_info.json`` inside the wheel with fields: cuda_version, gcc_version, build_flags, supported_archs. Runtime can read that and add a soft constraint on kernel selection.
Sam: for short term unblocking, reverting the kernel selector default to prefer fused-attn for seq<=1024 on hosts with older builds eliminated the latency regression in canary. But long-term let's finish reproducible CI.
Alex: thanks. Jin — assign yourself the pinning PR, Olga — CI smoke + fallback, Maria — wheel metadata and runtime check, Sam — cache and revert plan. I'll attach the failing job link in the PR.
ci-bot: Job #5823 failed: "flash-attn-wheel-build (ubuntu20.04/cuda11.1)" — https://ci.redwood.dev/5823 
Alex: thanks, coming up with the PRs now. We'll keep this thread for status updates. :spiral_calendar:
